data.title: Apple iPhone 18 Demand Signals Mixed Globally but Robust in U.S., Supporting Buy Rating
data.description:
Asiya Merchant, an analyst from Citi, maintained the Buy rating on Apple. The associated price target is $365.00.

Asiya Merchant has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors that indicate Apple’s iPhone franchise remains fundamentally robust despite mixed early signals for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. Week‑3 delivery data show U.S. order times holding up better than other regions, suggesting solid underlying demand in Apple’s largest and most profitable market.

In contrast, shorter wait times in China, India, and the U.K. hint at a milder upgrade cycle this year, but Merchant views this as partly timing‑related, with some buyers likely postponing purchases ahead of the iPhone Duo launch. Expert commentary cited in the analysis supports the view that any deferred demand could shift back toward the iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max once the broader lineup is available, reinforcing Apple’s long‑term earnings power and justifying a Buy recommendation.

data.title: Rivian Sell Rating Reiterated as Long-Term Risks Persist; Price Target Maintained at $14
data.description:
Analyst Andrew Percoco from Morgan Stanley maintained a Sell rating on Rivian Automotive and keeping the price target at $14.00.

Andrew Percoco has given his Sell rating due to a combination of factors related to Rivian’s long‑term execution risk and valuation versus its fundamentals. While the company delivered and produced materially more vehicles than expected in 3Q26 and kept its full‑year delivery guidance intact, he views the sustainability and mix of this strength as critical, particularly around the ramp of the R2 platform.

Percoco is concerned that if recent upside is driven mainly by R1 and EDV volumes, uncertainty around R2 scaling, profitability, and cash needs could continue to weigh on the equity story despite near‑term operational beats. With these strategic and financial risks still elevated, he maintains a cautious stance and reiterates a Sell rating, leaving his price target unchanged at $14.

data.title: Rajat Gupta CFA Maintains Sell Rating on Rivian, Keeps Price Target Unchanged at $15 Amid Capital-Intensive Growth and Demanding Valuation
data.description:
In a report released yesterday, Rajat Gupta CFA from J.P. Morgan maintained a Sell rating on Rivian Automotive, with a price target of $15.00.

Rajat Gupta CFA has given his Sell rating due to a combination of factors, despite acknowledging Rivian’s strong management, appealing products, and solid strategic partnerships. He expects the company to expand rapidly beyond 2025 but highlights that this growth path will require substantial capital, resulting in sizable cash outflows over the near term.

Rajat Gupta CFA’s rating is based on the view that Rivian’s valuation remains demanding when set against traditional automakers also investing in electrification. He notes that Rivian’s higher automotive enterprise value, coupled with current cash burn, means the market is assuming very robust long‑term cash generation, and he believes this risk-reward profile warrants an Underweight/Sell stance, even as he keeps the price target unchanged at $15.
